title: Gartner's top cybersecurity trends for 2026
body:
## Agentic AI is spreading inside companies faster than oversight can follow

Illustration: Quartz

Employees and developers are deploying agentic AI faster than the controls meant to govern it can be built, according to Gartner, and the result is a set of new attack surfaces that no one has assessed for risk. The firm points to no-code and low-code platforms, along with vibe coding, as the accelerants. [...] Gartner's term for the outcome is "unmanaged AI agent proliferation." It carries three linked problems: attack surfaces created outside any risk review, code that ships without standard security checks, and breaches of rules written on the assumption that someone is tracking how company data moves. [...] Michaels, a director analyst at Gartner, said companies now need to catalogue their existing encryption, phase it out and put new postquantum methods in its place, with cryptographic agility treated as a priority throughout. He added that organizations investing now will have their assets secured by the time quantum threats arrive.

title: Inside the Inference Hardware Revolution Of 2026 - IEEE Spectrum
body:
d-Matrix’s second-generation AI accelerator, Raptor, aims to improve inference performance by minimizing the distance between compute and memory. The GPUs in most current AI-inference deployments do this by placing high-bandwidth memory (HBM) around the perimeter of the GPU. Each HBM is a stack of DRAM dies linked together and connected to a superfast interface to the GPU. This is great for training, but for inference, the amount of memory you can stack this way and the bandwidth it can provide [...] Tensordyne is expected to accelerate AI inference with a logarithmic number system that leans on a property of logarithms: The log of A times B equals the log of A plus the log of B. So, storing numbers as their exponents lets the chip add where it would otherwise multiply. That matters in silicon because multiplier circuits draw more power and use more die area than adders do. Tensordyne says its rack-scale hardware, called Napier, can produce up to 1,300 tokens per second per user, and can do [...] Chris Philpot

d-Matrix’s Raptor removes that bottleneck by stacking an AI accelerator on a DRAM die. Instead of stacking memory, d-Matrix stacks memory and compute. Bhoja says this reduces the distance that data must travel to “micrometers instead of millimeters.” Like building a skyscraper, going vertical makes it possible to do more inside the same physical footprint.

body: # OpenAI strikes first news deal in Canada. Village Media, one of Canada's largest digital-only local news networks, is launching an AI-powered community services tool via a partnership with OpenAI. **Why it matters:** It marks OpenAI's first news deal in Canada. **Zoom in:** The partnership will see Village Media and OpenAI teaming up to launch Open Door, an AI-powered community health and care navigation platform. * The product is built by Village Media's Cares team, which leads community-support initiatives across its local markets. * The tool, which will launch in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, draws from a curated directory of more than 200 community organizations across 24 categories of support, per Village Media. **Between the lines:** While the product is built with support from OpenAI, Village Media owns Open Door, a spokesperson said. **Zoom out:** While OpenAI has long said efforts to partner with local news companies — including Axios — support its broader mission, it's worth noting that Big Tech platforms face intense scrutiny in Canada.

title: Rafa Flores - ADWEEK
body: ##### Chief Product Officer, Treasure Data. As Chief Product Officer at Treasure Data, Rafa Flores has spent 20 years across big tech as a self-described “fixer and builder.” It’s his unconventional journey with AI that’s rewriting how modern product teams operate. AI-native products are built with AI from day one, while AI-enabled products retrofit AI into existing systems. At Treasure Data, Flores is navigating both worlds simultaneously, shipping three new product lines in three months while maintaining their foundational data platform. When Flores’s team ships their Marketing Super Agent on December 2nd, sales enablement won’t see the final product until after launch. As big tech races to monetize AI, Flores believes vendors should focus on thought leadership first. Whether a CMO buys Treasure Data’s product or not, he’s willing to walk them through what an AI agent actually is. For marketing leaders feeling pressure from boards and bosses to “do something with AI,” the permission to ask basic questions might be the most liberating takeaway.

title: Flush With Cash From OpenAI, Opal Is Making an AI-Powered Audio Gadget - WIRED
body: # Flush With Cash From OpenAI, Opal Is Making an AI-Powered Audio Gadget. Opal, the company famous for making a fancy webcam, has pivoted to making other consumer electronics. Fueled by big investments from OpenAI and Samsung, it’s working on an audio gadget first. The company is changing its name to Opal Electronics.Courtesy of Opal Electronics. Opal Camera is rebranding to Opal Electronics and will expand its product portfolio beyond webcams to a broad range of consumer devices, some of which will be AI-focused. It's unclear whether it’s a wearable, though the source says it's a familiar product category, and that it's not designed to compete with the iPhone. Opal's audio product will launch in partnership with a specific AI lab—the source was unable to specify which—but Opal is in talks with OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, allowing users to switch models to their preference.

title: Republicans and Europe Agree: It’s Time to Make Life Easier for AI Companies - Gizmodo
body: The EU’s executive branch, the European Commission, announced on Wednesday that it wants to “simplify” its AI and privacy laws. The move is impacting two major pieces of European tech regulation that have had a global impact: the first-of-its-kind AI Act of 2024 and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), a comprehensive online privacy law that reshaped the internet when it passed in 2018. Under the proposed changes, tech companies will have more leeway to use anonymized user data to train their AI models. To be able to compete in this new global market, the EU must be able to fuel AI with high-quality data,” the Commission wrote while explaining the new changes.

title: The election that will shape the future of AI - Politico
body: # The election that will shape the future of AI. **Whether they fully appreciate it or not, Californians will be deciding on the future of global AI regulation** when they head to the voting booths on Tuesday. AI is a hot button issue across the world, but much of the national and international policy governing the technology still begins in California, where the most advanced AI labs are headquartered. Still, depending on who the next governor of California is, the state’s place in the firmament of global AI regulation could radically change. “[The election] will send a powerful signal to the middle powers in Canada, in the UK, in different EU member states who are treating Silicon Valley companies and tech companies with kid gloves because they see the U.S. as an important ally,” said Rishi Bharwani, the U.S. director for Reset Tech, which seeks more oversight of Big Tech.

title: Europe Is Bending the Knee to the US on Tech Policy - WIRED
body: Since the tariff agreement between the United States and Europe was signed last August, big tech companies, backed by the Trump administration, have increased pressure to soften restrictions on all fronts. The revision of net neutrality rules has disappeared from the version of the Digital Networks Act currently being worked on, while the initiative to rebalance market conditions between telecoms and big tech companies is ill-defined. “The current draft of the EU Space Act contradicts the spirit of the agreement,” the State Department wrote flatly, calling on Europe to “allow for smoother cooperation with the U.S. government and industry rather than introduce additional barriers to cooperation.” The European Commission continues to send letters to American tech giants calling on them to comply with the Digital Services Act (DSA) and the Digital Markets Act (DMA).

title: Zuckerberg warns against centralizing AI power - politico.com
body: ## STATE POLITICS & POLICY. STATE POLITICS & POLICY 4 items. ## GLOBAL POLITICS & POLICY. GLOBAL POLITICS & POLICY 4 items. Image 1: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg speaks during an event at the Biohub Imaging Institute in Redwood City, Calif., Wednesday, Nov. 5, 2025. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on Monday passionately defended the use of artificial intelligence, as the rapid advancement of the technology faces increased scrutiny — and calls for regulation — in the U.S. and globally. In a 6,500 word post timed to the announcement of his company’s new open source version of its own model, Muse Spark, Zuckerberg detailed his vision for AI, arguing the technology is not to be feared and pushing back on concerns that superintelligence could strip people of jobs. “It is also important that the US and its allies lead the open source AI ecosystem that will make up a large percent of global AI use,” Zuckerberg wrote.
